column3: The direct or indirect owners of the Mortgagors are permitted to obtain a mezzanine loan (the “Mezzanine Loan”) secured by the ownership interests in the Mortgagors subject to certain requirements, including, without limitation, the following: (a) the combined loan-to-value ratio of the Mortgage Loan is no higher than the loan-to-value ratio of the Mortgage Loan at loan origination, (b) the combined debt service coverage ratio of the Mortgage Loan is no lower than the debt service coverage ratio of the Mortgage Loan at loan origination, (c) an intercreditor agreement, and (d) a rating agency confirmation.

The Mortgaged Property is security for 9 senior pari passu notes aggregating $551,250,000 and 3 subordinate notes aggregating $23,750,000, totaling $575,000,000. The borrower has a leasehold interest in the Mortgaged Property pursuant to two ground leases: (i) a ground lease from Hillsborough County Aviation Authority for Parcel 1, comprising the majority of the mortgaged property, and (ii) a ground lease from IP Land Associates LLC for Parcel E, comprising the spaces currently occupied by Crate & Barrel and Ocean Prime. Both ground leases expire on December 31, 2080, with no extension options. The ground lessor has a right of first refusal (ROFR) if the ground lessee sells or assigns its interest in the leased premised. The ROFR is not extinguished by foreclosure; however, the ROFR does not apply to any assignment to or by any leasehold mortgagee or its nominee, or pursuant to a foreclosure or deed in lieu thereof.

The property condition report, dated October 6, 2025, identified immediate repairs and deferred maintenance costs which totaled $405,398.00 in the aggregate, for which the property condition report recommended a reserve of $420,893.34 but for which no escrow was established at origination. The Mortgage Loan documents require borrower to cause Tesla, Inc. to perform the repairs identified in the loan documents.

Michael Silberberg (“Silberberg Guarantor”) and Mark Karasick  (“Karasick Guarantor”), the non-recourse carveout guarantors of the Mortgage Loan, are defendants in the following ongoing  cases:  Silberberg Guarantor is a defendant in a foreclosure lawsuit commenced in 2021 in the Circuit Court of Cook County, Illinois (the “Cook County Case”), by a lender of a mortgage loan (unrelated to the Mortgage Loan) to a borrower for which Silberberg Guarantor is a guarantor where the loan went into a default during the COVID pandemic.
